7. **Capacity grew modestly by 1% in 2026Q2 compared to 2025Q2, while revenue passenger miles (RPMs) increased 1%, maintaining a load factor of 84.8%, slightly down 0.7 points from 85.5%.** Passenger mile yield rose 12% to 23.38 cents, reflecting strong pricing power amid fuel cost inflation. Fuel gallons consumed increased only 1% to 1.12 billion gallons [10-Q 2026-07-10 pp. 18-19].

8. **Delta led North American carriers in on-time arrival and departure performance in 2026Q2 and set a company record for domestic mishandled baggage rate, aided by proprietary AI baggage technology implemented at Atlanta.** The domestic mishandled baggage rate improved 50% in June 2026 versus the prior year baseline [8-K 2026-07-10].

9. **Fleet additions included delivery of 11 aircraft in 2026Q2, comprising A350-900, A321neo, and A220-300 models, supporting network expansion and replacement.** New daily nonstop service was launched from Los Angeles to Hong Kong and Chicago O’Hare, plus new international routes to Porto, Malta, Sardinia, and expanded service in Europe and Florida [8-K 2026-07-10].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

10. **Premium products continued to drive revenue growth, with premium ticket revenue up 17% year-over-year in 2026Q2, supported by investments in premium seats and corporate sales.** Main cabin unit revenue grew double digits for the second consecutive quarter. Loyalty and related revenue increased 19%, fueled by higher cardholder engagement and new credit card acquisitions, with American Express remuneration exceeding \$2.4 billion in 2026Q2 [10-Q 2026-07-10 pp. 7, 20; 8-K 2026-07-10].

11. **Cargo revenue surged 39% year-over-year, driven mainly by volume growth, while maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) revenue rose 32%, benefiting from increased work on legacy engine platforms and expanded third-party partnerships.** Miscellaneous revenue, including codeshare and joint venture settlements, increased 49% [10-Q 2026-07-10 pp. 20-22].

12. **Delta expanded its loyalty ecosystem with enhanced partnerships, including a decade-long renewal with Airbnb and new collaborations with The Wall Street Journal and Fox ONE, plus extended benefits for T-Mobile customers.** The loyalty program was ranked the world’s most valuable airline loyalty program by On Point Loyalty [8-K 2026-07-10].

### Labor Insights

13. **Salaries and related costs increased 8% in 2026Q2 to \$4.8 billion, driven by 4% base pay increases effective June 1, 2025 and June 1, 2026 for eligible employees and a 4% increase for pilots effective January 1, 2026.** Higher flight crew costs were also attributed to severe weather-related operational disruptions [10-Q 2026-07-10 p. 20; 10-Q 2026-04-08].

### Route Network Insights

14. **International passenger revenue increased 8% in 2026Q2, with growth across Atlantic, Latin America, and Pacific regions.** Atlantic revenue gains were driven by demand to London and European leisure markets; Latin America growth reflected Caribbean demand but was partially offset by reduced capacity to Mexico due to civil unrest earlier in 2026. Pacific revenue growth was supported by expanded capacity in South Korea through the Korean Air joint venture and increased China service [10-Q 2026-07-10 pp. 17-19].

15. **Delta placed significant aircraft orders in 2026Q1, including 30 Boeing 787-10s (deliveries starting 2031), 16 Airbus A330-900s, 15 A350-900s (deliveries starting 2029), and exercised options for 34 A321neos (deliveries starting 2029), supporting long-term fleet modernization and capacity planning.** Options remain for additional A321neos [10-Q 2026-07-10 p. 13].

### Wrap Up

In 2026Q2, Delta Air Lines demonstrated strong revenue growth across diverse streams, notably premium passenger services, cargo, loyalty, and third-party refinery sales, despite a modest 1% capacity increase. The surge in fuel prices—up 80% year-over-year—significantly pressured operating expenses and margins, resulting in a 26% decline in net income and a sharp contraction in free cash flow. Wage inflation and increased maintenance costs further elevated non-fuel costs. Operationally, Delta maintained high service levels with record on-time performance and baggage handling improvements, while expanding its fleet and network with new aircraft deliveries and international routes.

Management reaffirmed full-year guidance with expectations of mid-teens revenue growth and improved margins in the September quarter, projecting earnings per share between \$2.00 and \$2.50 and an operating margin of 11% to 13%. The company plans a 15% dividend increase beginning in 2026Q3 and continues debt reduction efforts to achieve gross leverage near 2x by year-end. No shares have been repurchased under the current buyback authorization through June 2028. Elevated fuel costs and geopolitical uncertainties remain key risks for the remainder of 2026.

2017.Q1:
### Financial Insights
1. **Net income decreased significantly.** United Airlines reported a net income of \$96 million for Q1 2017, down from \$313 million in Q1 2016, resulting in a diluted earnings per share of \$0.31 compared to \$0.88 the previous year. This decline highlights the challenges faced by the airline in maintaining profitability amid rising costs.

2. **Passenger revenue showed modest growth.** Passenger revenue increased by 2.6% year-over-year, reaching \$7.2 billion in Q1 2017, up from \$6.99 billion in Q1 2016. This growth indicates a slight improvement in demand for air travel, despite the overall decline in net income.

3. **Rising fuel costs impacted profitability.** Aircraft fuel costs surged by \$342 million, or 28.1%, compared to the same quarter in 2016. This significant increase in fuel expenses contributed to the overall decline in net income, emphasizing the volatility of fuel prices as a critical factor in airline profitability.

4. **Operating income fell sharply.** United reported an operating income of \$278 million for Q1 2017, down from \$650 million in Q1 2016. The increase in operating expenses, which rose to \$8.14 billion from \$7.55 billion, was a primary driver of this decline.

5. **Liquidity remains strong.** As of March 31, 2017, United Airlines maintained unrestricted liquidity of \$6.4 billion, including \$2 billion in undrawn commitments under its revolving credit facility. This robust liquidity position provides a buffer against operational challenges and financial uncertainties.

### Operational Insights
6. **Operational performance showed stability.** United achieved 25 zero-cancellation days during the first quarter, indicating a commitment to operational reliability. Consolidated traffic increased by 2.2%, while consolidated capacity rose by 2.6%, leading to a load factor of 79.6%. This suggests effective capacity management in response to demand.

7. **Fleet expansion continues.** During Q1 2017, United took delivery of two Boeing 787-9 aircraft, six Boeing 777-300ER, and one used Airbus A319 aircraft. This ongoing investment in fleet modernization reflects the airline's strategy to enhance operational efficiency and customer experience.

### Commercial Strategy Insights
8. **Share repurchase program executed.** United repurchased approximately 5 million shares of its common stock for \$0.3 billion during the first quarter. As of March 31, 2017, the company had \$1.5 billion remaining under its existing share repurchase authority, signaling confidence in its long-term value despite short-term financial pressures.

### Labor Insights
9. **Labor force remains stable.** As of March 31, 2017, United employed approximately 88,400 active employees, with about 80% represented by various U.S. labor organizations. The stability of the workforce is crucial for maintaining operational efficiency and service quality.

### Wrap Up
In Q1 2017, United Airlines faced significant challenges, reflected in a sharp decline in net income and operating income due to rising fuel costs and increased operational expenses. However, the airline demonstrated resilience with modest growth in passenger revenue and strong liquidity. Operational performance remained stable, supported by a commitment to fleet expansion and a proactive share repurchase strategy. While the financial outlook presents challenges, United's operational metrics and liquidity position provide a foundation for navigating the competitive airline landscape.
2017.Q2:
### Financial Insights

1. **Net income rose 39.1% year-over-year to \$818 million in 2017Q2, driven by an 8.3% increase in operating revenue and disciplined cost control excluding special charges.**  
   Passenger revenue for the quarter increased 6.4% to \$8.6 billion, with consolidated operating revenue reaching \$10.0 billion, up \$604 million or 6.4% from 2016Q2. Operating income grew 32.0% to \$1.4 billion, lifting operating margin to 14.0% from 11.3% a year earlier. Excluding special charges, operating income declined 3.4% and margin narrowed 1.5 points to 14.4%, reflecting higher labor and fuel costs. Diluted earnings per share increased 49.4% to \$2.66, or 5.4% on a non-GAAP basis excluding special charges and hedge adjustments. The improvement in net income was partly supported by a 6.9% reduction in diluted shares outstanding due to share repurchases [8-K 2017-07-18; 10-Q 2017-07-19].

2. **Fuel costs rose 16.1% year-over-year to \$1.67 billion, driven by a 13.2% increase in average price per gallon and modest 2.8% higher consumption, pressuring operating expenses.**  
   The average price per gallon of fuel increased to \$1.63 in the quarter (excluding hedge losses), compared to \$1.41 in 2016Q2, while total fuel consumption grew 2.8% to 1,023 million gallons. Mainline fuel consumption rose 4.0%, while regional fuel consumption declined 3.1%. Fuel expense as a percentage of operating expenses increased, contributing to a 3.2% rise in total operating expenses to \$8.6 billion. Excluding special charges, operating expenses increased 8.3%, with labor costs and fuel as main drivers [8-K 2017-07-18; 10-Q 2017-07-19].

3. **Labor costs increased 10.6% year-over-year due to higher pay rates and benefits from 2016 collective bargaining agreements and a 3.4% rise in average full-time equivalent employees, partially offset by lower profit sharing.**  
   Salaries and related costs rose by \$276 million compared to 2016Q2. Profit sharing expense declined 26.3% to \$154 million, reflecting lower payouts despite higher operating income. The average full-time equivalent workforce increased from 82,800 to 85,600 employees [10-Q 2017-07-19].

4. **Free cash flow fell sharply to \$314 million in 2017Q2 from \$1.78 billion a year earlier, reflecting a 62.6% increase in adjusted capital expenditures to \$1.25 billion and a 38.7% decline in operating cash flow.**  
   Capital expenditures rose due to timing changes in pre-delivery payments for future aircraft. Despite strong earnings, operating cash flow dropped from \$2.55 billion to \$1.56 billion. The company repurchased approximately 6 million shares for \$0.4 billion in the quarter and had \$1.1 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization as of June 30, 2017. Unrestricted liquidity was \$6.6 billion, including \$2.0 billion undrawn on its revolving credit facility [8-K 2017-07-18; 10-Q 2017-07-19].

### Operations Insights

5. **Capacity grew 4.2% year-over-year, with consolidated revenue passenger miles (RPMs) rising 4.3%, maintaining a stable load factor of 83.5%.**  
   Mainline operations accounted for most growth: mainline passengers increased 9.5% to 28.1 million, mainline RPMs rose 5.7% to 50.6 billion, and available seat miles (ASMs) increased 5.3% to 60.5 billion. Regional operations saw declines in passengers (-5.7%) and RPMs (-6.0%). Average stage length decreased slightly, reflecting network adjustments. Cargo ton miles grew 21.9%, contributing to a 22.1% increase in cargo revenue, which reached \$254 million [8-K 2017-07-18; 10-Q 2017-07-19].

6. **Fleet expanded modestly with 3.9% more mainline aircraft, including deliveries of six Boeing 777-300ER, ten Embraer E175, and one used Airbus A319 aircraft in the quarter.**  
   The mainline fleet grew from 720 to 748 aircraft, while regional aircraft increased from 494 to 515. United deferred four Airbus A350 deliveries out of 2018 and accelerated Boeing 737 MAX and 787-10 aircraft deliveries into 2019. The company converted 100 Boeing 737 MAX orders to the larger MAX 10 variant, expecting deliveries starting late 2020. Average daily utilization of mainline aircraft increased slightly to 10 hours 46 minutes [8-K 2017-07-18; 10-Q 2017-07-19].

7. **Operational reliability improved, with United reporting the best completion, on-time departure, and arrival performance among major U.S. carriers in the quarter.**  
   Completion factor reached 99.5%, and on-time departure performance was 64.5%, up 4.6 points year-over-year. These operational improvements contributed to lower cancellations and customer disruptions, supporting customer experience initiatives [8-K 2017-07-18].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

8. **Passenger unit revenues (PRASM) increased 2.1% year-over-year, driven by a 2.0% yield increase, despite a 0.1-point decline in load factor.**  
   Mainline PRASM rose 2.7%, with yields up 2.3%. Domestic PRASM increased 2.4%, Atlantic 3.3%, and Latin America 7.8%, while Pacific PRASM declined 5.5%, reflecting "incremental weakness" in China and Hong Kong markets due to supply and demand imbalances. United enhanced MileagePlus award availability and introduced new award charts effective November 1, aiming to boost loyalty engagement [8-K 2017-07-18; 8-K 2017-07-11; 10-Q 2017-07-19].

9. **United expanded international and domestic route offerings, including new nonstop service between Newark and Buenos Aires, and Los Angeles and Singapore—the longest nonstop U.S. flight.**  
   The airline added a second daily flight between Newark and Bogota, increased service and upgauged aircraft from San Francisco to 18 destinations, and expanded service to Hawaii on 11 routes, offering more flights between the mainland and Hawaiian Islands than any other carrier. The company also restructured Houston George Bush Intercontinental Airport operations to shorten connection times starting in October [8-K 2017-07-18].

### Labor Insights

10. **Labor relations reflected finalized 2016 collective bargaining agreements, resulting in higher wages and benefits that increased labor costs, while operational performance bonuses totaled \$28 million.**  
    The workforce grew 3.4% year-over-year to 85,600 full-time equivalents. The company did not report any labor disruptions in the quarter. Profit sharing declined despite higher operating income, partially offsetting increased wage and benefit expenses [8-K 2017-07-18; 10-Q 2017-07-19].

### Route Network Insights

11. **United’s network remained broad with service to 338 airports on five continents, operating approximately 4,500 daily flights, supported by a mainline fleet of 748 aircraft and 515 regional jets.**  
    The company’s Star Alliance membership provides access to over 190 countries. Capacity growth focused on domestic markets and selective international expansion, while the Pacific region experienced softness impacting unit revenue growth [8-K 2017-07-18; 10-Q 2017-07-19].

### Corporate Insights

12. **United maintained strong liquidity and credit facilities, with \$6.6 billion unrestricted liquidity including \$2.0 billion undrawn revolver capacity, and managed debt with \$238 million in principal repayments in the quarter.**  
    In March 2017, United entered a new \$1.5 billion term loan due 2024 and a \$2.0 billion revolving credit facility, replacing prior credit agreements. The revolving credit facility was fully available at quarter-end. The company had \$1.1 billion remaining under its share repurchase authorization. Risks disclosed include exposure to fuel price volatility, labor costs, regulatory changes, and geopolitical factors, consistent with prior filings [8-K 2017-07-18; 10-Q 2017-07-19].

---

### Wrap Up

In 2017Q2, United Airlines reported solid financial gains with net income rising 39%, supported by revenue growth and controlled cost increases excluding special charges. However, rising fuel prices and labor costs pressured margins, while free cash flow declined sharply due to higher capital spending. Operationally, United expanded its mainline fleet, improved reliability metrics, and grew capacity modestly, maintaining a stable load factor. Commercially, unit revenues improved except in the Pacific region, where demand softness in China and Hong Kong was noted. Labor costs increased in line with negotiated pay rises, but no labor disruptions were reported. The network continued to broaden with new long-haul routes and enhanced domestic service. Liquidity remained strong with ample revolving credit availability and ongoing share repurchases.

**Guidance:** United projected third-quarter 2017 pre-tax margins between 12.5% and 14.5%, with capacity growth around 4%, and expected consolidated PRASM to range roughly from flat to a slight decline compared to 2016Q3. Fuel consumption was forecast near 1.08 billion gallons with an average price per gallon around \$1.63. Capital expenditures were expected to remain elevated due to aircraft deliveries and associated pre-delivery payments [8-K 2017-07-18; 8-K 2017-07-19]. No material labor disputes or regulatory actions were disclosed for the near term.
2017.Q3:
### Financial Insights

1. **Third-quarter 2017 net income declined 34% year-over-year to \$637 million, pressured by severe weather disruptions and rising costs.**  
   United reported net income of \$637 million (\$2.12 diluted EPS) in 3Q17, down from \$965 million (\$3.01 diluted EPS) in 3Q16. The company attributed an estimated \$185 million reduction in pre-tax income to flight cancellations caused by severe weather in southeast Texas, Florida, and the Caribbean, which led to about 8,300 canceled flights. Excluding special charges and hedge adjustments, net income was \$669 million (\$2.22 diluted EPS) versus \$997 million (\$3.11 diluted EPS) in 3Q16 [8-K 2017-10-18; 10-Q 2017-10-19].

2. **Operating income and margin contracted sharply due to higher fuel and labor costs amid flat revenue.**  
   Operating income fell 32.8% to \$1.1 billion, with operating margin declining 5.3 points to 11.1%. Total operating revenue was essentially flat at \$9.9 billion (-0.4%), including a \$210 million estimated revenue loss from weather disruptions. Passenger revenue decreased 0.9% to \$8.5 billion. Cargo revenue grew 14.7% to \$257 million, driven by higher international freight volume. Operating expenses rose 6.0% to \$8.8 billion, driven primarily by a 12.9% increase in fuel expense (+\$206 million) and a 7.1% rise in salaries and related costs (+\$187 million), partly offset by lower profit sharing expense (-36.3%) and reduced aircraft rent (-13.7%) [8-K 2017-10-18; 10-Q 2017-10-19].

3. **Unit costs rose due to fuel price increases and higher labor expenses despite operational efficiency gains.**  
   Consolidated cost per available seat mile (CASM) increased 3.0% year-over-year to 12.54 cents, with CASM excluding fuel, profit sharing, third-party business expenses, and special charges rising 2.6%, mainly due to higher labor costs. Fuel price per gallon increased 11.8% to \$1.70, contributing significantly to the 12.9% increase in fuel expense. Profit sharing per available seat mile declined 38.2%, reflecting lower incentive expenses. Depreciation and amortization increased 10.5%, reflecting fleet additions and accelerated depreciation [8-K 2017-10-18; 10-Q 2017-10-19].

4. **Liquidity remained strong at \$6.3 billion with continued share repurchases totaling \$556 million in the quarter.**  
   United ended 3Q17 with \$6.3 billion in unrestricted liquidity, including \$2.0 billion of undrawn revolving credit capacity. The company raised \$400 million in unsecured debt at a 4.25% interest rate and made \$222 million in debt and capital lease principal payments during the quarter. Share repurchases totaled \$556 million (approximately 8 million shares), with \$553 million remaining under the current buyback authorization [8-K 2017-10-18; 10-Q 2017-10-19].

5. **Capital expenditures increased to \$1.1 billion in the quarter, reflecting fleet investment and technology upgrades.**  
   Capital spending was \$1.1 billion in 3Q17, up from \$0.7 billion in 3Q16. The company took delivery of one Boeing 787-9, four Boeing 737-800, and nine Embraer E175 aircraft during the quarter, continuing fleet modernization and expansion [10-Q 2017-10-19].

### Operations Insights

6. **Capacity grew 3.0% with traffic growth of 1.7%, leading to a load factor of 84.4%, down slightly from the prior year.**  
   Available seat miles (ASM) increased 3.0% year-over-year to 63.2 billion, while revenue passenger miles (RPM) rose 1.7% to 53.5 billion. The resulting load factor decreased by about 1.3 points to 84.4%. Mainline capacity rose 4.2%, with mainline RPM up 3.2%, while regional operations saw capacity decline 7.2% and RPM fall 1.8%. Average stage length decreased 3.0% for mainline operations, reflecting network adjustments [8-K 2017-10-18; 10-Q 2017-10-19].

7. **Operational performance reached record third-quarter on-time departures despite disruptions from multiple hurricanes.**  
   United achieved its best-ever third-quarter consolidated on-time departure performance. The company credited employee efforts for maintaining operations through severe weather events including Hurricanes Harvey and Irma. Employees earned \$11 million in operational bonuses for the quarter [8-K 2017-10-18; 8-K 2017-10-10].

8. **Fleet size increased 3.7% to 1,240 aircraft, with continued modernization focused on mainline and regional jets.**  
   The mainline fleet grew 3.7% to 751 aircraft, including deliveries of Boeing 787-9, 737-800, and Embraer E175 jets. Regional aircraft operated by United Express carriers totaled 489 at quarter-end. The company plans to retire its Boeing 747-400 fleet, with the final flight scheduled for November 7, 2017 [8-K 2017-10-18; 10-Q 2017-10-19].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

9. **Passenger unit revenue declined 3.7% year-over-year, pressured by Basic Economy rollout, ULCC pricing, and weather impacts.**  
   Consolidated passenger revenue per available seat mile (PRASM) fell 3.7% to 12.17 cents. Domestic PRASM declined 4.4%, Pacific international markets suffered a 10.4% PRASM decrease, while Latin America grew 3.5%. The company noted that Basic Economy introduction and aggressive ultralow-cost carrier (ULCC) pricing in hub markets contributed to revenue pressure. Weather disruptions also negatively affected unit revenues by approximately one point [8-K 2017-10-18].

10. **Cargo revenue grew 14.7% to \$257 million, driven by higher international freight volumes amid network expansion.**  
    Cargo ton miles increased 16.2%, with United leveraging its global network and Star Alliance membership to expand freight capacity and revenue [8-K 2017-10-18].

### Labor Insights

11. **Salaries and related costs rose 7.1% due to higher pay rates, benefits from 2016 labor agreements, and a 2.6% increase in employees.**  
    The increase in labor expense was partially offset by lower profit sharing and incentive expenses. Average full-time equivalent employees increased from 85.1 thousand to 87.3 thousand year-over-year. The company finalized multiple collective bargaining agreements in 2016, which contributed to higher pay and benefit costs in 3Q17 [10-Q 2017-10-19; 8-K 2017-10-18].

### Route Network Insights

12. **Network adjustments included incremental capacity growth focused on domestic hubs and selective international markets.**  
    United's capacity growth of approximately 3.0% for the quarter reflected a 4.5% increase in domestic capacity and a 2.0% increase in international capacity year-over-year. The company continued to optimize its network, including re-banking hubs such as Houston (IAH) for better connectivity and introducing new routes like Newark to Buenos Aires and Los Angeles to Singapore [8-K 2017-07-18; 8-K 2017-10-18].

---

### Wrap Up

United Airlines’ 2017 third quarter was marked by operational resilience amid severe weather disruptions that reduced pre-tax income by about \$185 million and led to 8,300 canceled flights. Despite a 3% increase in capacity and record operational on-time performance, revenue fell slightly due to weather impacts and competitive pressure from Basic Economy and ULCCs, resulting in a 3.7% decline in passenger unit revenue. Rising fuel prices and labor costs pushed consolidated unit costs up 3%, compressing operating margins and net income by over 30%. The company maintained strong liquidity at \$6.3 billion, continued fleet modernization with new aircraft deliveries, and returned \$556 million to shareholders through share repurchases.

Guidance for full-year 2017 anticipated capacity growth of roughly 3.5%, with adjusted pre-tax margins between 10.0% and 10.5%, and a consolidated PRASM decline of up to 4%. The company planned capital expenditures near \$4 billion and expected continued investments in network optimization, including hub re-banking and international route adjustments. No material changes in labor relations or regulatory risks were disclosed for the quarter.
2017.Q4:
### Financial Insights

1. **Fourth-quarter 2017 revenue rose 4.3% to \$9.4 billion, driven by passenger and cargo growth, but full-year net income declined 5.8% to \$2.1 billion.**  
   United's Q4 passenger revenue increased 4.1% year-over-year to \$8.08 billion, with mainline passenger revenue up 4.6% and regional up 2.2%. Cargo revenue surged 21.6% to \$304 million, attributed primarily to higher international freight volume and yields. Total operating revenue for 2017 was \$37.7 billion, up 3.2%. Despite revenue growth, full-year net income declined from \$2.3 billion in 2016 to \$2.1 billion in 2017, a 5.8% decrease, reflecting higher costs [8-K 2018-01-23].

2. **Operating expenses grew 8.2% in Q4 2017, with fuel costs up 20.6% due to higher prices; labor costs also increased significantly.**  
   Total operating expenses in Q4 were \$8.7 billion, up \$662 million or 8.2% year-over-year. Aircraft fuel expense was \$1.875 billion, a 20.6% increase driven by higher average fuel prices (\$1.91 per gallon in Q4 2017 vs. \$1.62 in Q4 2016) and slightly higher consumption. Salaries and related costs rose 5.3% to \$2.7 billion, reflecting labor agreements ratified in 2016. Excluding fuel, profit sharing, special charges, and third-party expenses, unit costs per available seat mile (CASM) increased 1.5% in Q4 and 3.1% for the full year, mainly due to labor expense growth [8-K 2018-01-23; 10-K 2018-02-22].

3. **Consolidated unit revenue per available seat mile (PRASM) was flat (+0.2%) in Q4 but declined slightly (-0.4%) for the full year, impacted by international softness and competitive pressures.**  
   Q4 consolidated PRASM increased marginally by 0.2% compared to Q4 2016. Mainline PRASM was up 0.3%, and regional PRASM rose 1.0%. Domestic PRASM was flat, Atlantic PRASM increased 1.3%, but Pacific PRASM declined 2.9%. For the full year, consolidated PRASM declined 0.4%. Management attributed softness partly to weakness in China/Hong Kong and Guam markets and competitive pricing actions, including the rollout of Basic Economy fares and Ultra Low-Cost Carrier pricing [8-K 2018-01-23; 8-K 2017-11-08].

4. **Pre-tax margin contracted to 6.4% in Q4 2017 from 9.8% in Q4 2016, reflecting cost pressures despite revenue gains; adjusted pre-tax margin excluding special charges was 6.7%.**  
   Income before income taxes was \$600 million in Q4 2017, down 32.1% from \$884 million in Q4 2016. Excluding special charges and hedge adjustments, pre-tax margin was 6.7% versus 9.5% in the prior year quarter. For the full year, pre-tax margin was 7.9%, down 2.5 points from 10.4% in 2016 [8-K 2018-01-23].

5. **United completed a \$2.0 billion share repurchase program in 2017 and authorized a new \$3.0 billion program in December; year-end unrestricted liquidity was \$5.8 billion.**  
   In 2017, UAL repurchased approximately 28 million shares for \$1.8 billion. The company ended the year with \$5.8 billion in unrestricted liquidity, including cash, equivalents, short-term investments, and available credit facility capacity. Capital expenditures totaled \$4.0 billion for the year, with adjusted capital expenditures of \$4.7 billion, reflecting investments including those acquired through debt and capital leases [8-K 2018-01-23].

### Operations Insights

6. **Capacity grew 4.0% in Q4 2017, with passenger traffic rising 3.1%, causing load factor to decline 0.7 points to 81.7%.**  
   Available seat miles (ASMs) increased 4.0% year-over-year to 65.0 billion, while revenue passenger miles (RPMs) grew 3.1% to 53.1 billion. The load factor fell to 81.7% from 82.4%, driven by capacity growth outpacing demand. Domestic load factor held steady at 85.2%, but international load factor declined 1.7 points to 77.2%, reflecting softness in certain international markets [8-K 2018-01-23].

7. **Fleet size expanded modestly, ending 2017 with 1,262 aircraft, a 2.5% increase, including mainline and regional aircraft additions.**  
   The mainline fleet grew from 1,214 to 1,240 aircraft (2.1% increase) and regional fleet from 494 to 517 (4.7% increase). United took delivery of new aircraft including Boeing 787-9s, Boeing 737-800s, and Embraer E175s during the year, supporting capacity growth and network expansion [8-K 2018-01-23; 10-Q 2017-10-19].

8. **United achieved record operational reliability in 2017, including best-ever on-time departures, fewest cancellations, and best baggage handling performance.**  
   The company reported its best operational year since the 2010 merger, with record completion factors and on-time performance in the fourth quarter, despite challenging weather events. This operational improvement contributed to better cost control and customer experience [8-K 2018-01-23].

### Route Network Insights

9. **United expanded its domestic and international network with 44 new domestic routes and 13 new international routes announced in 2017.**  
   The airline increased nonstop service from six hubs to nine ski destinations and added service to Hawaiian Islands from multiple hubs, offering more nonstop flights to Hawaii than any competitor. New international routes included seasonal service from San Francisco to Papeete, Tahiti, starting in October 2018 [8-K 2018-01-23].

### Labor Insights

10. **Labor costs increased due to ratified agreements in 2016, with profit sharing payouts declining 44.4% year-over-year in 2017 to \$349 million.**  
    Salaries and related costs rose 7.5% year-over-year, reflecting labor agreements. Profit sharing expense decreased significantly from \$628 million in 2016 to \$349 million in 2017, reducing overall labor costs in the year but contributing to higher unit costs excluding profit sharing. Employees earned \$349 million in profit sharing for 2017 despite the reduction [8-K 2018-01-23].

### Wrap Up

United Airlines’ fourth quarter of 2017 showed revenue growth supported by increased passenger and cargo volumes, but cost pressures—especially from fuel and labor—compressed margins and limited net income growth for the full year. Capacity expansion outpaced traffic growth, leading to a modest decline in load factor, particularly internationally. Operational reliability reached record levels, which management highlighted as a foundation for improving customer experience and cost control. The company completed a sizeable share repurchase program and maintained strong liquidity while investing heavily in fleet and network expansion, including new domestic and international routes.

For first-quarter 2018, United guided to flat to modestly positive unit revenue growth (0% to +2%) and a capacity increase of 3.5% to 4.5%, with pre-tax margins expected near zero. Cost per available seat mile excluding fuel and special items was projected to be flat to up 1%, while fuel prices were expected to rise, increasing overall operating costs. The company also anticipated no profit sharing expense in Q1 2018, reflecting the timing of payouts. No material operational disruptions or legal events were disclosed for the period ending December 31, 2017.
2017.FY:
### Financial Insights

1. **United Airlines’ 2017 net income declined slightly to \$2.1 billion, with EPS up modestly to \$7.02 despite a 0.4% PRASM decrease**  
   For the full year ended December 31, 2017, United reported net income of \$2.1 billion, a 5.8% decrease from \$2.26 billion in 2016, while diluted earnings per share rose 2.5% to \$7.02 due to an 8.1% reduction in weighted average diluted shares outstanding (330.3 million to 303.6 million) [10-K filed 2018-02-22]. The company’s consolidated passenger revenue per available seat mile (PRASM) declined 0.4% year-over-year, reflecting pressure on unit revenue despite a 3.5% capacity increase [10-K filed 2018-02-22]. Total revenue grew 3.2% to \$37.7 billion, helped by a 18.2% increase in cargo revenue [8-K filed 2018-01-23].

2. **Fuel expense rose sharply by 18.9% due mainly to higher fuel prices, increasing total operating costs and unit costs**  
   Aircraft fuel expense increased 18.9% to \$6.9 billion in 2017 from \$5.8 billion in 2016, driven primarily by a 16.8% rise in average fuel price per gallon to \$1.74, while fuel consumption rose modestly by 1.9% [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. This fuel cost increase contributed to a 2.8% rise in consolidated cost per available seat mile (CASM), and a 3.1% increase in CASM excluding special charges, third-party business expenses, fuel, and profit sharing [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. The company notes that fuel prices remain volatile and a \$1 change in crude oil price would impact annual fuel expense by approximately \$95 million [10-Q filed 2017-07-19].

3. **Labor costs increased 7.5% year-over-year, reflecting higher wages and profit sharing; profit sharing expense declined sharply but employees earned \$349 million in total profit sharing**  
   Salaries and related costs rose 7.5% to \$11.0 billion [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. However, profit sharing expense decreased 44.4% to \$349 million [8-K filed 2018-01-23], consistent with lower pre-tax earnings. Employees earned \$349 million in profit sharing for 2017 [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. Excluding fuel, profit sharing, special charges, and third-party business expenses, CASM increased 3.1%, mainly due to labor agreements ratified in 2016 [8-K filed 2018-01-23].

4. **Operating margin compressed to 8.4% excluding special charges, down 3.8 points from 2016, reflecting cost pressures and revenue challenges**  
   The company reported a 2017 pre-tax margin of 7.9%, down 2.5 points from 2016. Adjusted pre-tax margin excluding special charges and hedge adjustments was 8.4%, a 3.8-point decline [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. Operating income fell 1.9% to \$11.0 billion [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. The margin compression was driven by higher fuel and labor costs, partially offset by revenue growth and share repurchases reducing share count [8-K filed 2018-01-23].

5. **United repurchased \$1.8 billion of common stock in 2017, completing a \$2.0 billion program and authorizing a new \$3.0 billion buyback**  
   In 2017, UAL repurchased approximately 28 million shares for \$1.8 billion, completing the \$2.0 billion program authorized in July 2016. In December 2017, the Board authorized a new \$3.0 billion repurchase program with \$3.0 billion remaining as of year-end [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. Share repurchases contributed to a reduction in diluted shares outstanding by 8.1% year-over-year [8-K filed 2018-01-23].

6. **United ended 2017 with \$5.8 billion in unrestricted liquidity, supported by a \$2.0 billion revolving credit facility fully available at mid-year**  
   Unrestricted liquidity at year-end was \$5.8 billion, comprising cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments, and available credit capacity [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. As of June 30, 2017, the company had \$6.6 billion unrestricted liquidity including \$2.0 billion undrawn revolver capacity [10-Q filed 2017-07-19]. The company refinanced its term loans in March 2017 with a \$1.5 billion term loan due 2024 and a \$2.0 billion revolving credit facility due 2022, fully available as of September 30, 2017 [10-Q filed 2017-10-19].

7. **Capital expenditures rose to approximately \$4.7 billion (non-GAAP adjusted) in 2017, reflecting fleet investments and infrastructure, resulting in negative free cash flow**  
   Adjusted capital expenditures totaled \$4.7 billion for the full year 2017, up from \$3.3 billion in 2016 [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. Net cash provided by operating activities was \$3.4 billion, resulting in negative free cash flow of approximately \$1.3 billion after capital spending [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. The company also acquired aircraft through issuance of debt and capital leases [8-K filed 2017-07-18].

### Operations Insights

8. **Capacity grew 3.5% in 2017 while consolidated load factor declined 0.5 points to 82.4%, with international load factor falling 1.1 points**  
   United increased available seat miles (ASM) by 3.5% in 2017 to 262.4 billion [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. Consolidated load factor declined from 82.9% to 82.4%, driven by a 1.1-point decrease in international load factor to 78.9% [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. Domestic load factor remained relatively flat at 85.2% [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. Revenue passenger miles (RPM) increased 2.8% to 216.3 billion [8-K filed 2018-01-23].

9. **Passenger revenue growth was concentrated in mainline (+4.5%) and cargo (+18.2%), while regional passenger revenue declined 3.2%**  
   Mainline passenger revenue increased 4.5% to \$26.6 billion, while regional passenger revenue fell 3.2% to \$5.9 billion [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. Cargo revenue surged 18.2% to \$1.04 billion, driven by higher international freight volumes and yields [8-K filed 2018-01-23].

10. **Fleet size increased modestly with mainline aircraft up by 5 units to 742 and regional aircraft up by 21 to 515, reflecting deliveries of new Boeing 777-300ER and Embraer E175s**  
    The mainline fleet grew from 737 to 742 aircraft, including deliveries of six Boeing 777-300ERs, one used Airbus A319, and ten Embraer E175s in Q2 2017 [8-K filed 2017-07-18]. Regional fleet increased from 494 to 515, with additions of CRJ200s and Embraer E175s, offset by retirements of ERJ 145 and CRJ 700 aircraft [8-K filed 2017-07-18]. The company deferred four Airbus A350 deliveries from 2018 and accelerated Boeing 737 MAX deliveries into 2019 and 2020 [8-K filed 2017-07-18].

11. **Operational reliability improved significantly, with record on-time departures, fewest cancellations, and best baggage handling in company history**  
    United reported record-setting operational reliability in 2017, including best-ever on-time departure performance, fewest cancellations, and best baggage handling [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. For example, November 2017 had the fewest cancellations in company history and record on-time arrival rates [8-K filed 2017-12-07]. These operational improvements were achieved despite weather disruptions in southeast Texas, Florida, and the Caribbean that caused about 8,300 flight cancellations in Q3 2017, reducing income before taxes by an estimated \$185 million [10-Q filed 2017-10-19].

### Labor Insights

12. **Workforce expanded modestly with average full-time equivalent employees increasing 3.1% to 86.2 thousand, while labor agreements ratified in 2016 contributed to higher labor costs**  
    The average number of full-time equivalent employees grew from 83.6 thousand in 2016 to 86.2 thousand in 2017 [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. Labor agreements ratified in 2016 increased expenses, contributing to a 3.1% rise in CASM excluding fuel and profit sharing [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. Employees earned \$349 million in profit sharing for 2017 despite a 44.4% decline in profit sharing expense [8-K filed 2018-01-23].

### Route Network Insights

13. **United’s network remained extensive with approximately 4,500 daily flights to 338 airports on five continents, anchored by seven U.S. mainland hubs**  
    United operated approximately 4,500 daily flights to 338 airports worldwide in 2017 [10-K filed 2018-02-22]. The airline’s hubs included Chicago, Denver, Houston, Los Angeles, Newark/New York, San Francisco, and Washington, D.C. [8-K filed 2017-07-11]. United was a founding member of Star Alliance, providing connectivity to over 190 countries through 28 member airlines [8-K filed 2017-07-11]. The fleet and capacity increases supported network growth, especially on international long-haul routes.

14. **Pacific region faced incremental weakness due to unfavorable supply and demand dynamics in China and Hong Kong, impacting unit revenue**  
    The Pacific region underperformed relative to other regions in 2017, with reported weakness attributed to supply and demand challenges in China and Hong Kong [8-K filed 2017-07-11]. This contributed to a 2.9% decline in Pacific PRASM in Q4 2017 and a 4.3% drop in Pacific passenger revenue compared to 2016 [8-K filed 2018-01-23].

### Wrap Up

In 2017, United Airlines expanded capacity and fleet size modestly while navigating a challenging revenue environment marked by a slight decline in unit revenue and significant fuel price increases. Despite revenue growth in mainline passenger and cargo segments, regional passenger revenue declined. Higher fuel and labor costs compressed margins, resulting in a lower adjusted pre-tax margin compared to 2016. The company maintained strong liquidity and completed a \$1.8 billion share repurchase program, initiating a new \$3.0 billion authorization. Operational reliability improved markedly, achieving record on-time performance and fewer cancellations even amid weather disruptions. The Pacific region remained a weak spot due to market dynamics in China and Hong Kong. Labor costs rose in line with new agreements, with workforce size increasing moderately.

For the first quarter of 2018, United guided to capacity growth of 3.5% to 4.5%, flat to 2.0% consolidated PRASM growth, and flat to 1.0% non-fuel CASM growth, with a target pre-tax margin near zero percent [8-K filed 2018-01-23]. The company also planned to continue share repurchases under the new authorization and expected stable operational performance. No material litigation, fatal accidents, or labor disruptions were disclosed for 2017.

2018.Q1:
### Financial Insights

1. **United Airlines grew revenue but faced margin pressure from higher fuel costs in 2018Q1.**  
   Total operating revenue increased 7.2% year-over-year to \$9.0 billion, driven by a 6.5% rise in passenger revenue to \$8.1 billion and a 23.1% increase in cargo revenue to \$293 million [8-K 2018-04-17; 10-Q 2018-04-18]. However, operating income declined 13.8% to \$276 million, and operating margin fell 0.7 points to 3.1% due to a 26.0% surge in aircraft fuel expense (+\$405 million to \$1.965 billion) and a 15.5% increase in regional capacity purchase costs [8-K 2018-04-17; 10-Q 2018-04-18]. Consolidated unit cost per available seat mile (CASM) rose 4.3% to 14.13 cents, with fuel expense per ASM increasing 21.9% [8-K 2018-04-17]. Excluding special charges, third-party business expenses, fuel, and profit sharing, CASM was nearly flat (+0.6%) year-over-year at 10.82 cents, indicating stable core operating costs aside from fuel and profit sharing effects [8-K 2018-04-17].

2. **Profitability improved modestly on a net income basis despite operating margin decline, aided by share repurchases and lower tax rate.**  
   Net income was \$147 million in 2018Q1, up 48.5% from \$99 million in 2017Q1, and diluted EPS rose 62.5% to \$0.52 [8-K 2018-04-17]. Excluding special charges and mark-to-market (MTM) gains on equity investments, net income increased 8.3% to \$143 million and diluted EPS 19.0% to \$0.50 [8-K 2018-04-17]. The effective cash tax rate was approximately 0.5% over the prior twelve months, substantially lower than prior years, which contributed to improved net income [8-K 2018-04-17; 10-Q 2018-04-18]. The weighted average diluted shares outstanding declined 9.4% year-over-year to 284.9 million due to share repurchases; UAL repurchased approximately 8.4 million shares for \$0.6 billion in 1Q18 and had \$2.4 billion remaining under its program [10-Q 2018-04-18; 8-K 2018-04-17].

3. **Cash flow generation strengthened significantly with free cash flow turning positive after prior-year deficit.**  
   Net cash provided by operating activities increased to \$1.733 billion from \$547 million in 2017Q1 [8-K 2018-04-17]. Capital expenditures rose 41.7% to \$979 million, but adjusted capital expenditures (which exclude fully reimbursable projects) declined 25.2% to \$1.013 billion [8-K 2018-04-17]. Free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital expenditures) was \$720 million positive in 1Q18 versus a negative \$807 million in 1Q17 [8-K 2018-04-17]. After financing activities, free cash flow net of financings was \$754 million positive, reversing a prior-year negative \$144 million [8-K 2018-04-17].

4. **Capital allocation included fleet investment and share repurchases, with ongoing fleet modernization.**  
   UAL took delivery of six new widebody aircraft in 1Q18—four Boeing 787-9s and two Boeing 777-300ERs [10-Q 2018-04-18; 8-K 2018-04-17]. The company announced plans to introduce the Boeing 737 MAX 9 domestically starting June 2018 and agreed to purchase 20 used Airbus A319 aircraft for delivery in 2020-2021 [8-K 2018-04-17]. Aircraft rent expense declined 29.1% year-over-year to \$130 million in 1Q18 due to lease expirations and aircraft purchases [10-Q 2018-04-18]. The company continued share repurchases, spending \$747 million year-to-date through April 16, 2018 [8-K 2018-04-17].

### Operations Insights

5. **Capacity and traffic growth supported revenue gains with improved load factor.**  
   Consolidated capacity (available seat miles, ASM) rose 3.6% year-over-year, while consolidated traffic (revenue passenger miles, RPM) increased 4.7%, lifting the load factor to 80.4% in 1Q18 [10-Q 2018-04-18; 8-K 2018-04-17]. Mainline ASM grew 3.3% and RPM 4.6%, while regional ASM increased 6.3% and RPM 5.7% [8-K 2018-04-17]. Load factor gains reflected stronger demand relative to capacity growth.

6. **Passenger revenue per ASM (PRASM) and yield increased modestly, with regional operations showing slightly higher growth.**  
   Mainline PRASM rose 2.8% year-over-year to 12.07 cents; regional PRASM increased 1.1% to 21.35 cents [8-K 2018-04-17]. Average yield per revenue passenger mile increased 1.6% for mainline and 1.7% for regional operations [8-K 2018-04-17]. These unit revenue improvements contributed to the 6.5% overall passenger revenue growth.

7. **Fuel consumption rose slightly but was outweighed by higher fuel prices driving fuel cost increases.**  
   Fuel gallons consumed increased 1.3% to 771 million, while the average price per gallon rose 22.9% to \$2.09 for mainline operations [8-K 2018-04-17]. Consolidated average fuel price per gallon was \$2.11 in 1Q18, up from \$1.70 in 1Q17 [8-K 2018-04-17].

8. **Fleet size expanded modestly with deliveries of new aircraft and regional fleet growth.**  
   The mainline fleet grew 0.9% to 750 aircraft, including the addition of six new widebodies [8-K 2018-04-17]. The regional fleet increased by 36 aircraft to 554, reflecting capacity growth initiatives to improve hub connectivity [8-K 2018-04-17; 10-Q 2018-04-18]. Average daily utilization of aircraft increased 2.1% to nearly 10 hours [8-K 2018-04-17].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

9. **Passenger revenue growth was broad-based across mainline and regional, domestic and international markets.**  
   Mainline passenger revenue grew 6.2% to \$6.6 billion; regional passenger revenue rose 7.5% to \$1.5 billion [8-K 2018-04-17]. Domestic passenger revenue increased 6.8%, Atlantic international revenue surged 12.1%, Pacific revenue rose 1.5%, and Latin America revenue grew 3.4% [10-Q 2018-04-18]. PRASM gains were strongest on Atlantic routes (+8.8%) and Latin America (+5.1%) [10-Q 2018-04-18].

10. **Ancillary fees, including baggage and ticket change fees, contributed steadily to passenger revenue.**  
    Ancillary fees recorded within passenger revenue were \$497 million in 1Q18, up slightly from \$478 million in 1Q17 [10-Q 2018-04-18].

11. **United continued to enhance customer experience and expand network offerings.**  
    The company announced new international service including Houston-Sydney and Denver-London, and year-round San Francisco-Auckland service starting April 2019 [8-K 2018-04-17]. It introduced United Premium Plus, a premium cabin product for select international flights [8-K 2018-04-17]. United eliminated second checked bag fees on all North America to China/Hong Kong routes [8-K 2018-04-17].

### Labor Insights

12. **Salaries and related costs rose moderately on higher pay rates and workforce growth.**  
    Salaries and related costs increased 3.4% year-over-year to \$2.726 billion, driven by higher pay rates under collective bargaining agreements and a 0.5% increase in full-time equivalent employees [10-Q 2018-04-18]. Profit sharing expense declined, contributing to stable non-fuel unit costs [8-K 2018-04-17].

### Wrap Up

In 2018Q1, United Airlines expanded revenue through capacity growth and improved unit revenues, particularly in international markets, supported by a modestly larger fleet and higher utilization. However, a sharp rise in fuel prices and increased regional capacity costs pressured operating margins and drove up unit costs. Despite this, net income and earnings per share improved significantly due to lower tax rates and share repurchases reducing diluted share count. Operating cash flow strengthened markedly, enabling positive free cash flow after capital investments in new aircraft and ongoing share repurchases. United also advanced its network and product offerings, including new international routes and premium cabin enhancements, while labor costs rose modestly in line with wage agreements and staffing.

**Guidance and Outlook:**  
United's investor updates projected 2018 consolidated capacity growth of approximately 4.5% to 5.5% and expected a pre-tax margin (adjusted) of 9.0% to 11.0% for the full year [8-K 2018-04-17]. Consolidated PRASM was forecasted to increase 1.0% to 3.0%, with non-fuel CASM excluding special charges expected to be flat to down 1.0% year-over-year [8-K 2018-04-17]. The company planned continued share repurchases and fleet modernization, including introduction of Boeing 737 MAX 9 aircraft and used Airbus A319 acquisitions [8-K 2018-04-17]. No material operational disruptions, labor disputes, or regulatory risks were disclosed for 1Q18.
2018.Q2:
### Financial Insights

1. **Second-quarter 2018 revenue rose 7.7% year-over-year to \$10.8 billion, driven by an 8.0% increase in passenger revenue to \$9.9 billion.** Cargo revenue increased 15.0% to \$314 million, and other operating revenue remained flat at \$583 million compared to 2017. Passenger revenue per available seat mile (PRASM) increased 3.0%, and total revenue per available seat mile (TRASM) rose 2.8%. These gains occurred alongside a 4.8% increase in consolidated capacity measured by available seat miles (ASM) [8-K filed 2018-07-17; 10-Q filed 2018-07-18].

2. **Operating expenses grew 12.2% to \$9.6 billion, with aircraft fuel costs up 43.2% (\$721 million) due to a 38.7% increase in fuel price per gallon and capacity growth of 4.8%.** Salaries and related costs increased 1.3% (\$36 million) mainly from higher pay rates and benefits under collective bargaining agreements and a 0.8% rise in average full-time equivalent employees. Regional capacity purchase costs rose 24.0% (\$132 million) primarily from increased regional flying to improve domestic hub connectivity and rate adjustments under capacity purchase agreements. Aircraft rent decreased 21.7% (\$33 million) due to aircraft purchases and lease expirations [10-Q filed 2018-07-18].

3. **Consolidated unit costs per available seat mile (CASM) increased 7.1% year-over-year to 13.60 cents, substantially driven by fuel cost increases.** However, CASM excluding special charges, third-party business expenses, fuel, and profit sharing declined slightly by 0.4%, reflecting underlying cost control efforts. Profit sharing expense per ASM fell by 30.4% [8-K filed 2018-07-17].

4. **Net income for Q2 2018 was \$684 million, down 16.7% from \$821 million in Q2 2017, with diluted earnings per share decreasing 7.1% to \$2.48.** Excluding special charges and mark-to-market losses on equity investments, net income rose to \$889 million with diluted EPS of \$3.23, indicating that special items materially affected GAAP earnings. Pre-tax margin was 8.0%, down 4.8 points from 12.8% in 2017, while adjusted pre-tax margin excluding special charges improved to 10.4% from 13.2% a year earlier [8-K filed 2018-07-17].

5. **United repurchased approximately 5.9 million shares for \$407 million during Q2 2018, with \$2.0 billion remaining under the share repurchase program as of June 30, 2018.** Year-to-date through June 30, 2018, 14.3 million shares were repurchased for \$1.0 billion [10-Q filed 2018-07-18].

6. **Capital expenditures in the first half of 2018 were \$1.7 billion, slightly below \$1.8 billion in the prior year period, mainly for new aircraft, improvements, and IT/facility assets.** Adjusted capital expenditures (excluding non-cash and fully reimbursable projects) were \$783 million in Q2 2018, down 37.2% versus \$1.2 billion in Q2 2017. Free cash flow net of financings improved significantly to \$1.7 billion in Q2 2018 from \$472 million a year earlier [10-Q filed 2018-07-18].

7. **The company recorded a special non-cash impairment charge in Q2 2018 related to the full write-off of intangible assets associated with Brazil route authorities.** This followed the ratification of the Brazil–United States open skies agreement, which removed traffic restrictions and impaired the asset’s value. The impaired asset is not pledged as collateral on borrowings [8-K filed 2018-07-06].

### Operations Insights

8. **Consolidated traffic (revenue passenger miles, RPM) increased 6.4% while capacity (ASM) grew 4.8% in Q2 2018, leading to a load factor of 84.8%, an improvement over the prior year.** Mainline passengers rose 5.4%, and cargo ton miles increased 3.3%. The airline completed its best-ever second-quarter on-time departure performance and ranked first among largest competitors in this metric [10-Q filed 2018-07-18; 8-K filed 2018-07-17].

9. **Fuel consumption increased 3.4% to 1,058 million gallons in Q2 2018, driven by capacity growth, while the average fuel price per gallon rose 38.7% to \$2.26.** This sharp rise in fuel price was the primary driver of the 43.2% increase in fuel expense [8-K filed 2018-07-17].

10. **Fleet additions in early 2018 included deliveries of four Boeing 787-9s and two Boeing 777-300ERs in Q1, plus one 777-300ER and six Boeing 737 MAX 9 aircraft in Q2, making United the North American launch customer for the 737 MAX 9.** The 737 MAX 9 began service in June 2018, offering improved fuel efficiency. The total mainline fleet increased from 744 aircraft at year-end 2017 to 768 by mid-2018, with regional aircraft growing from 518 to 554 [10-Q filed 2018-07-18; 8-K filed 2018-07-17].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

11. **Passenger revenue growth was supported by a 3.0% increase in PRASM, with domestic PRASM up 1.7% and international PRASM gains concentrated in Atlantic markets (+8.8%) and Latin America (+5.1%), while Pacific PRASM declined 1.5%.** Ancillary fees within passenger revenue increased modestly to \$497 million from \$478 million in Q1 2018 [10-Q filed 2018-04-18; 8-K filed 2018-07-17].

12. **United expanded its customer experience offerings with new Polaris lounges opened in San Francisco, Newark, and Houston during Q2 2018, and extended live DIRECTV streaming entertainment to all Wi-Fi equipped aircraft.** The airline also introduced the United Explorer Card with enhanced benefits and travel credits [8-K filed 2018-07-17].

13. **Network growth focused on domestic hubs, with capacity growth guidance for 2018 narrowed to 4.5%-5.0%, mostly concentrated in mid-continent hubs to enhance connectivity and rebanking.** This strategy aims to increase connection opportunities and optimize off-peak flying [10-Q filed 2018-07-18; 8-K filed 2018-04-17].

### Labor Insights

14. **Salaries and related costs increased modestly by 1.3% in Q2 2018, reflecting contractual pay rate increases from collective bargaining agreements and a 0.8% rise in average full-time equivalent employees.** The workforce increase was slight, consistent with capacity growth. Profit sharing expense per ASM declined significantly, contributing to underlying cost containment [10-Q filed 2018-07-18].

### Route Network Insights

15. **United announced new international service expansions including year-round San Francisco–Auckland service starting April 2019, daily Houston–Havana flights pending DOT authority, and new nonstop Auckland–Chicago service by Air New Zealand as part of the joint venture.** Domestic route additions included new flights connecting six hubs to eight destinations in several U.S. states [8-K filed 2018-04-17].

### Wrap Up

United Airlines’ 2018 second quarter demonstrated solid top-line growth with an 8.0% increase in passenger revenue and a 7.7% rise in total operating revenue, supported by capacity expansion and improved load factors. However, a steep 43.2% jump in fuel costs, driven by a 38.7% increase in fuel prices, pressured margins and contributed to a 7.1% rise in unit costs (CASM). Excluding fuel and special items, underlying unit costs declined slightly, reflecting operational efficiencies and cost control. Net income declined on a GAAP basis due to special charges, including a significant impairment of Brazil route assets following regulatory changes, but adjusted earnings per share rose. Operationally, United achieved its best second-quarter on-time performance, expanded its fleet with fuel-efficient aircraft, and focused on enhancing connectivity at domestic hubs through rebanking and network growth. The company also continued share repurchases and maintained strong free cash flow generation despite elevated capital expenditures for fleet and infrastructure. Labor costs rose modestly in line with contractual agreements, while commercial initiatives such as Polaris lounges and ancillary services supported revenue growth. United’s 2018 capacity growth guidance was narrowed to 4.5%-5.0%, emphasizing domestic hubs and off-peak utilization.

**Guidance Overview:**  
For full-year 2018, United narrowed its capacity growth forecast to 4.5%-5.0%, with expected PRASM growth of 1.0%-3.0% for Q2 and a full-year adjusted diluted EPS range raised to \$7.25-\$8.75, excluding special charges and mark-to-market adjustments. Fuel price assumptions increased slightly to about \$2.21-\$2.26 per gallon for Q2. The company expects non-fuel CASM excluding special charges, third-party business expenses, fuel, and profit sharing to be flat to down 1.0% for the year, reflecting ongoing productivity initiatives [8-K filed 2018-07-17; 8-K filed 2018-04-17; 10-Q filed 2018-07-18]. No material labor disputes, operational disruptions, or regulatory risks beyond the Brazil route asset impairment were disclosed for the period.
2018.Q3:
### Financial Insights

1. **Third-quarter 2018 net income rose 30% year-over-year to \$836 million, with adjusted diluted EPS up 36% to \$3.06**  
   United Airlines reported net income of \$836 million in 3Q18 versus \$645 million in 3Q17, and diluted earnings per share (EPS) increased from \$2.15 to \$3.06. Adjusted net income and adjusted diluted EPS, which exclude special charges, mark-to-market equity investment gains/losses, and interest expense on certain capital leases, were \$837 million and \$3.06, respectively, representing a 23.6% and 36.0% increase year-over-year. The company’s effective tax rate dropped significantly to 21.2% in 3Q18 from 35.0% in 3Q17, reflecting the impact of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act [8-K 2018-10-16; 10-Q 2018-10-17].

2. **Passenger revenue grew 11.6% to \$10.1 billion driven by 7.2% traffic growth and a 1.6 point load factor increase**  
   Passenger revenue increased by \$1.1 billion from the prior year quarter, primarily due to a 7.2% rise in revenue passenger miles (RPMs) and a 1.6 point increase in load factor (percentage of seats filled). Consolidated passenger revenue per available seat mile (PRASM) rose 6.1%, exceeding the high end of guidance (4%-6%). Yield, or average fare per revenue passenger mile, increased 4.1% year-over-year, supported by strong close-in bookings and premium cabin demand, especially on domestic and Atlantic routes [8-K 2018-10-16; 10-Q 2018-10-17].

3. **Operating expenses increased 11.9%, led by a 42.2% surge in fuel costs and 5.2% higher salaries and related costs**  
   Operating expenses rose \$1.0 billion to \$9.8 billion, with aircraft fuel expense up \$763 million (42.2%) mainly due to a 36.5% increase in average fuel price per gallon and a 5.1% capacity increase. Salaries and related costs increased \$145 million (5.2%) driven by contractually higher pay rates, benefits from collective bargaining agreements, and a 1.9% rise in average full-time equivalents. Regional capacity purchase costs rose 16.9% (\$96 million) due to increased regional flying and rate increases. Distribution expenses increased 13.3% (\$50 million) primarily from higher credit card fees tied to increased passenger revenue [10-Q 2018-10-17].

4. **Consolidated cost per available seat mile (CASM) rose 6.4%, but CASM ex-fuel, special charges, third-party expenses, and profit sharing declined 0.4%**  
   The GAAP CASM increased from 12.50 to 13.30 cents, reflecting higher fuel prices and other costs. However, the adjusted CASM excluding fuel, special charges, third-party business expenses, and profit sharing decreased slightly by 0.4% to 9.31 cents, indicating some operational cost control despite the fuel headwind. Profit sharing costs declined 9.5% per ASM [8-K 2018-10-16].

5. **Capital expenditures totaled \$858 million in 3Q18, down from \$1.12 billion in 3Q17, with adjusted capital expenditures of \$807 million**  
   Capital spending primarily funded new aircraft, improvements, and IT assets. Adjusted capital expenditures exclude assets acquired through debt issuance, airport construction financing, and fully reimbursable projects. For the nine months ended September 30, 2018, adjusted capital expenditures were \$2.6 billion versus \$3.7 billion in 2017 [8-K 2018-10-16; 10-Q 2018-10-17].

6. **Free cash flow was positive \$98 million in 3Q18 on a non-GAAP basis, improving from a negative \$505 million in 3Q17**  
   Net cash from operations was \$905 million, less adjusted capital expenditures of \$807 million. Year-to-date free cash flow was \$2.5 billion, a significant improvement over the prior year. The company repurchased 0.5 million shares for \$34 million in 3Q18, completing 14.8 million shares for \$1.0 billion over nine months, with \$2.0 billion remaining under its repurchase program [8-K 2018-10-16].

7. **Adjusted pre-tax margin was 9.7%, slightly down from 10.5% in 3Q17, reflecting strong revenue offset by cost pressures**  
   Pre-tax income was \$1.1 billion, with an adjusted pre-tax margin of 9.7% versus 10.5% a year earlier. Despite a 6.1% PRASM increase, margin compression was due to higher fuel and salary costs. The company recaptured approximately 100% of the year-over-year fuel expense increase through higher revenue [8-K 2018-10-16].

### Operations Insights

8. **Capacity grew 4.2% in 3Q18, with mainline available seat miles (ASMs) increasing from 63.2 billion to 65.8 billion**  
   Passenger traffic (RPMs) rose 6.1% to 56.8 billion, resulting in a load factor improvement of 1.4 points. The increase in capacity was partly driven by growth at mid-continent hubs Chicago (ORD), Denver (DEN), and Houston (IAH), which together saw 9.7% capacity growth and led the system in unit revenue gains. Regional ASMs grew 13.7%, reflecting expanded regional flying to improve hub connectivity [10-Q 2018-10-17; 8-K 2018-10-16].

9. **Mainline fleet size was approximately 760 aircraft, with 546 regional aircraft operated by United Express carriers**  
   United continued fleet modernization with deliveries including one Boeing 777-300ER, six Boeing 737 MAX 9s in 3Q, and plans for additional deliveries in 4Q18 and beyond. The company also announced orders for 25 Embraer E-175s and 13 Boeing 787-9s, with total capital commitments of \$23.8 billion, including \$1.1 billion due in the last quarter of 2018 [8-K 2018-10-16; 10-Q 2018-10-17].

10. **Operational performance set records with best-ever on-time departures in 2Q18 and strong completion factors at key hubs in 3Q18**

Load factors reached record levels in July 2018 [8-K 2018-07-17; 8-K 2018-10-16].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

11. **Strong premium cabin and close-in bookings drove PRASM growth, with domestic PRASM up 6.7% and Atlantic PRASM up 7.1% year-over-year**  
    The company highlighted improved premium cabin demand in the Atlantic and Pacific markets and strong close-in demand domestically. Latin America PRASM declined 3.4%, pressured by markets like Cancun, Argentina, and Brazil. United also enhanced customer experience with a new boarding process at 1,000 gates globally and launched the United Corporate Preferred travel program [8-K 2018-10-16].

12. **United’s MileagePlus loyalty program and Polaris lounges received industry recognition**  
    MileagePlus was voted Favorite Frequent-Flyer Program in the Trazee Awards, and the United Polaris lounge at Chicago O’Hare was named Best Business Class Lounge in the U.S. by Skytrax. The company also redesigned its website homepage to improve personalization [8-K 2018-10-16].

### Labor Insights

13. **Salaries and related costs increased 5.2% in 3Q18, driven by collective bargaining agreements and a 1.9% rise in full-time equivalent employees**

### Route Network Insights

14. **United expanded international routes including nonstop service from Washington Dulles to Tel Aviv and San Francisco to Amsterdam**  
    The airline announced new international services subject to government approval, including seasonal service from Newark to Naples and Prague. It also added 100 flights daily to top U.S. ski destinations for the 2018/2019 season and increased seats to popular college football towns and for the Consumer Electronics Show [8-K 2018-10-16].

### Wrap Up

United Airlines’ third quarter 2018 showed a substantial increase in net income and earnings per share, driven by strong passenger revenue growth from higher traffic, load factors, and premium cabin demand. This revenue growth fully offset a significant increase in fuel costs, which rose over 40% year-over-year, and contributed to a modest margin compression. Operating expenses grew mainly due to fuel, salaries, and increased regional flying to support hub connectivity. Capacity grew moderately, led by mid-continent hubs, while operational performance set company records in on-time departures and completion factors. The airline maintained robust free cash flow and continued share repurchases. United also advanced its fleet modernization with new aircraft deliveries and orders, alongside network expansion into new international routes. Labor costs rose consistent with collective bargaining agreements.

For the remainder of 2018, United guided to capacity growth of about 5%, PRASM growth of 3% to 5%, and a slight increase or flat non-fuel CASM excluding special charges, with adjusted pre-tax margins expected between 5% and 7%. The company anticipates recovering approximately 90% of the full-year fuel cost increase through revenue initiatives, signaling continued focus on balancing growth and cost control amid higher fuel prices [8-K 2018-10-16; 8-K 2018-07-17; 10-Q 2018-10-17].
2018.Q4:
### Financial Insights

1. **Fourth-quarter 2018 net income declined 20% year-over-year amid higher fuel costs, but adjusted earnings expanded.**  
   UAL reported Q4 net income of \$462 million, down from \$579 million in Q4 2017, with diluted EPS falling 14.1% to \$1.70. Pre-tax earnings were \$556 million with a 5.3% margin, down 1.3 points from the prior year. Adjusted net income, which excludes special charges, mark-to-market (MTM) impacts, and other adjustments, was \$657 million, up 56.4%, driving adjusted diluted EPS to \$2.41, a 67.4% increase over Q4 2017. Adjusted pre-tax margin expanded 0.9 points to 7.8%. The decline in GAAP earnings reflects \$301 million in special charges, including a \$206 million impairment related to Hong Kong routes, while adjusted results show underlying profitability improvements [8-K 2019-01-15].

2. **Passenger revenue grew 11.3% in Q4 2018, driven by a 5.0% PRASM increase and 6.0% capacity growth.**  
   Passenger revenue totaled \$9.56 billion, up from \$8.59 billion in Q4 2017. Consolidated passenger revenue per available seat mile (PRASM) increased 5.0%, reaching the high end of guidance. Capacity, measured by available seat miles (ASM), expanded 6.0%, resulting in a slight decrease in yield (+3.8%) but higher overall revenue. Domestic passenger revenue rose 12.8% with PRASM up 6.0% on 6.4% ASM growth. International passenger revenue increased 8.8% with a 3.2% PRASM gain on 5.4% capacity growth. The Atlantic and Pacific segments showed mixed yield trends, with Atlantic yield down 5.0% but PRASM up 1.6%, and Pacific yield up 3.2% with 4.0% ASM growth [8-K 2019-01-15].

3. **Operating expenses rose sharply, primarily due to a 26.9% increase in fuel costs, but core cost per ASM declined slightly.**  
   Total operating expenses increased 13.4% to \$9.84 billion in Q4 2018. Aircraft fuel expense was \$2.38 billion, up 26.9% from \$1.88 billion in Q4 2017, reflecting higher fuel prices (average \$2.30/gallon in Q4 vs. \$1.91 in Q4 2017) and a 5.7% increase in fuel gallons consumed. Salaries and related costs increased 9.2% to \$2.92 billion, driven by wage growth and benefit expenses. Consolidated cost per available seat mile (CASM) increased 7.0% to 14.28 cents, but CASM excluding special charges, third-party business expenses, fuel, and profit sharing declined 0.7% to 10.22 cents, indicating underlying cost control [8-K 2019-01-15].

4. **Free cash flow turned negative in Q4 due to higher capital expenditures, despite strong operating cash flow.**  
   Net cash provided by operating activities was \$1.10 billion in Q4 2018, up 51% from \$728 million in Q4 2017. However, capital expenditures rose to \$1.59 billion from \$1.10 billion, resulting in a negative free cash flow of approximately \$483 million (Non-GAAP). Adjusted capital expenditures, which exclude non-cash items and reimbursable projects, increased to \$1.58 billion from \$1.05 billion. For the full year 2018, free cash flow was positive at \$1.99 billion, recovering from a negative \$1.32 billion in 2017 [8-K 2019-01-15].

5. **Share repurchases continued with \$1.2 billion spent in 2018 and \$1.8 billion remaining authorization.**  
   UAL repurchased approximately 17.5 million shares during 2018 for \$1.2 billion. As of December 31, 2018, \$1.8 billion remained under the share repurchase program [10-K 2019-02-28].

### Operations Insights

6. **Capacity increased 6.0% in Q4 2018, with revenue passenger miles (RPMs) growing 6.4% and load factor steady at 83.6%.**  
   UAL’s available seat miles (ASM) grew 4.9% for the full year 2018, with RPMs up 6.4%, yielding an improved load factor of 83.6% versus 82.4% in 2017. In Q4, consolidated traffic (RPM) increased 6.9% year-over-year, while capacity grew 6.4%, lifting load factor by 0.4 points. The average stage length remained stable at about 1,426 miles. Fuel gallons consumed increased 5.7% in Q4 2018 compared to Q4 2017 [8-K 2019-01-09, 10-K 2019-02-28].

7. **Fleet additions included 21 new Boeing aircraft delivered in 2018 and new orders placed in December.**  
   During 2018, UAL took delivery of 21 Boeing jets: four 777-300ER, four 787-9, three 787-10, and ten 737 MAX 9 aircraft. In December 2018, the airline ordered an additional four 777-300ER and 24 737 MAX aircraft. UAL operated approximately 770 mainline and 559 regional aircraft at year-end 2018 [8-K 2019-01-15, 8-K 2018-10-16].

8. **Operational reliability improved with best-ever completion rates and on-time departures.**  
   UAL set company records in 2018 for the most revenue passengers flown, most mainline departures, and fewest cancellations. Completion factor reached 99.2% (up from 99.0% in 2017), and the U.S. Department of Transportation on-time arrival rate was 79.8% (down slightly from 81.9% in 2017). The fourth quarter achieved top-tier on-time departure performance among major competitors, including the peak holiday season [8-K 2019-01-15].

### Commercial Strategy Insights

9. **Strong pricing and premium cabin demand supported revenue growth despite fuel headwinds.**  
   Domestic PRASM increased 6.0% in Q4, led by higher close-in yields and leisure demand. International PRASM rose 3.2%, with Pacific routes recovering and Latin America showing modest yield growth. The introduction of United Premium Plus premium economy seating and expanded personal device entertainment were notable product initiatives. The MileagePlus loyalty program earned several awards, including Best Overall Frequent-Flyer Program for the 15th consecutive year [8-K 2019-01-15, 8-K 2018-10-16].

10. **Network expansion included 93 new routes added in 2018 and significant growth at mid-continent hubs.**  
    UAL introduced more new routes than any other U.S. airline in 2018, including new nonstop international services from San Francisco to Toronto, Melbourne, New Delhi, Seoul, Auckland, Tahiti, and Amsterdam, pending government approvals. Mid-continent hubs in Chicago, Denver, and Houston grew capacity by 9.7% in Q3 and led the system in unit revenue growth [8-K 2019-01-15, 8-K 2018-10-16].

### Labor Insights

11. **Labor costs rose due to wage increases and benefit expenses, partially offset by lower incentive payouts.**  
    Salaries and related costs increased 9.2% in Q4 2018 to \$2.92 billion, driven by collective bargaining agreements and wage growth. Average full-time equivalent employees rose 2.0% to 87,300. Employees earned \$334 million in profit sharing for 2018, slightly below 2017 levels. The full implementation of the flight attendant joint collective bargaining agreement was completed in 2018, allowing for improved operational efficiency [8-K 2019-01-15, 10-K 2019-02-28].

### Wrap Up

In the fourth quarter of 2018, United Airlines experienced solid revenue growth driven by increased capacity and higher unit revenues, particularly in domestic markets and premium cabins. However, the sharp rise in fuel prices—26.9% higher year-over-year in Q4—significantly pressured operating expenses and constrained GAAP earnings, which declined 20%, although adjusted earnings showed meaningful improvement. Operationally, the airline expanded its fleet and network, achieving record completion rates and on-time performance. Labor costs increased in line with wage agreements but were partially offset by stable profit sharing. Capital expenditures accelerated, resulting in negative free cash flow for the quarter despite strong operating cash generation.

UAL's strategic focus on network growth, premium product offerings, and operational reliability contributed to record passenger volumes and revenue gains, while cost control measures helped contain unit costs excluding fuel. The company ended 2018 with strong liquidity, ongoing share repurchases, and a positive outlook for adjusted earnings growth in 2019.

**Guidance for 2019:** UAL forecasted consolidated capacity growth of 4.0% to 6.0%, flat to modest PRASM growth of up to 3.0%, and flat or better non-fuel CASM excluding special items. The company expected adjusted pre-tax margins of 2.5% to 4.5% and adjusted diluted EPS between \$10.00 and \$12.00. Fuel price assumptions ranged from \$2.00 to \$2.05 per gallon, with estimated fuel consumption of 965 to 985 million gallons [8-K 2019-01-15, 8-K 2019-01-16]. No material operational disruptions or regulatory risks were disclosed for 2018Q4.

United Airlines’ 2018 financial and operational performance was marked by solid revenue growth and capacity expansion, with load factor improvement and record operational reliability metrics. Rising fuel prices significantly increased operating costs, limiting net income growth despite effective revenue recovery strategies. Capacity (available seat miles, ASM) grew 5.9%, outpacing traffic (revenue passenger miles, RPM) growth of 6.5%, causing load factor to be 80.9%, down 0.5 points [10-Q 2019-04-17; 8-K 2019-04-16].

The company managed to keep unit costs nearly flat on a GAAP basis despite wage inflation and modest cost pressures in distribution and landing fees. Fleet modernization and network expansion continued, supporting improved load factors and revenue per unit metrics, while operational reliability remained strong amid industry challenges such as the Boeing 737 MAX grounding.

Liquidity and cash generation remained robust, supporting significant capital expenditures and a continued aggressive share repurchase program, highlighted by a new \$3 billion authorization. Labor costs increased with headcount and contractual wage growth, with profit sharing reflecting the improved earnings environment.
